clue.text: Fake map, one covering US city

indicators.note: covering something means lying over it on every side, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a chart is a map, especially for sailors
LA is Los Angeles
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A forged map of an American city is passed off as genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake' is the definition here, a noun meaning an impostor, not an adjective describing the map.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is an impostor who claims skills they lack, so a fake in the sense of a person.

clue.text: Source of light awkwardly balanced on 14

indicators.note: something placed awkwardly sits out of its proper order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
14 across is ARTIST, and RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A lamp is precariously balanced on top of a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 14 across, ARTIST, which here stands for its abbreviation RA, placed after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabra is a branched holder for several candles, so it is a source of light.

clue.text: Actor with basic moves? These are more elaborate moves

indicators.note: letters that make moves shift position, so the preceding words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor makes simple gestures, and the follow-up says fancier ones exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moves' appears twice: first as the signal to rearrange, then as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatics are gymnastic feats such as somersaults and balancing, far more elaborate physical moves than an actor's basic ones.

clue.text: What's offered in school is lesson material

indicators.note: what is offered inside the following words is a run of letters sitting within them

parts.note: the run straddles the end of school, all of is and the start of lesson

explanation.surface: A school claims its lesson content is the curriculum material on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves, so a kind of material.

clue.text: Internet threat, item remaining to be picked up before start of year

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ort is a scrap of food left over after a meal, an old word crosswords love
January is the year's first month

explanation.surface: Some lingering bit of online malware waits to be collected before New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts you toward a sound-alike, but in a down clue it means lifted, so ORT reads upward as TRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trojan is malicious software disguised as something harmless, named after the wooden horse of Troy.

clue.text: Ironing out source of disagreement in description of airship

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of disagreement

explanation.surface: Smoothing out the cause of a household quarrel, like who does the ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-rigid airship, or blimp, keeps its shape by gas pressure alone with no internal frame, so the term describes such a craft.

clue.text: Church taking risk, trimmed tree from biblical land

indicators.note: something trimmed has had its end cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to dare is to take a risk

explanation.surface: A church gambles on a pruned tree imported from the Holy Land.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar of Lebanon is the tree repeatedly praised in the Bible, so it is a tree from a biblical land.

clue.text: Chap I have going round America is having an effect

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a man, a chap
the contraction I've
the United States of America

explanation.surface: A man boasts that his travels around America are making a difference.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat is old jazz slang for a man, and the contraction I've splits around the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Causative means producing a result, acting as a cause, so it describes something having an effect.

clue.text: Gloomy day on rescue vessel

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A dismal day spent aboard a lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark and gloomy are synonyms for lacking light, and both also describe a depressed mood.

clue.text: Operates historic site, perhaps, closing off central section

indicators.note: closing off the middle section of a site shuts out its centre, so the middle letter is dropped

parts.note: ruins are an example of a historic site, as perhaps signals

explanation.surface: A heritage body manages a monument but closes the middle part to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or machine is to operate it, so the third-person forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Number provided by computer's last logic circuit

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the final letter of computer

explanation.surface: A figure is supplied by a computer's final circuit component.
explanation.definitionFit: A NOR gate is an electronic logic circuit that outputs true only when all inputs are false.

clue.text: Uranium, now stolen, sadly restricts researcher's latest contribution to fission

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem something in, so the jumble encloses the next piece
sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
taken as written

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its most recent, final letter

parts.note: the final letter of researcher

explanation.surface: A news story: uranium has been stolen, frustrating a scientist's nuclear research.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow, or thermal, neutrons are the particles most readily absorbed by uranium-235, triggering the fission in a reactor.

clue.text: Changes in climate? Blame representative

indicators.note: changes made to the words that follow alter their arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Climate change? Hold our elected representative responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes in climate' reads as a single phrase, but 'Changes in' is the signal and 'representative' is the adjective definition, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Emblematical means serving as an emblem or symbol, so it is representative of something.

clue.text: With servant around, one left on depressing journey

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the servant's word wraps the rest

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left
grim means dismal or depressing

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned on a miserable trip with only a servant for company.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey to a sacred place, so it is a specific kind of journey.

clue.text: Blokes pursuing seabird to be brought into international custody

indicators.note: being brought into something means going inside it, so the pair sit within the abbreviation

parts.note: Int. is the abbreviation for international

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the men come after the bird

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Men chase a seabird and end up held by an international authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for international is split open to take in the bird and the men.
explanation.definitionFit: Internment is the confinement of people, often in wartime, without trial, a form of custody.

clue.text: Performer, tenor, is in role (not lead)

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the following word
without its lead the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A singer, the tenor, is cast in a supporting role rather than as the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not lead' sounds like a supporting role on stage, but it removes the first letter of the word for role.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist can be any performer, as in a recording artist or variety artiste.

clue.text: State capital having no love for religious rite

indicators.note: having none of something means that piece is taken away

parts.note: Sacramento is the capital of California
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A state capital that does not care for church ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament, such as baptism or communion, is a Christian religious rite.

clue.text: Ex-soldier? I will have mostly nasty one in prison

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the final word

parts.note: the can is slang for prison

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written
vile means nasty
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A former soldier confesses to keeping a very nasty person in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will' looks like the contraction I'll, but 'will have' merely joins. The question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has left the army returns to being a civilian, a person not in the armed forces.

clue.text: That chap will take on advertising industry to make a point

parts.note: he is that chap
Adland is an informal name for the advertising world

explanation.surface: A man joins the advertising business to prove his point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a point' reads as arguing; here a point is a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a promontory jutting into the sea, and point is a common name for one, as in Lizard Point.

clue.text: Unexpected change in direction from company acquired by wealthy alien

indicators.note: acquired by means taken in, so the company goes inside

parts.note: rich means wealthy
Co. is short for company
ET is the extraterrestrial from the film

explanation.surface: A business switches course sharply after a rich extraterrestrial buys it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a rebound of a bullet or stone off a surface, an abrupt deflection from its path.

clue.text: Gathering to have silver initially loaded on board famous ship

indicators.note: having things on board means carrying them inside

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of loaded

explanation.surface: Treasure is loaded aboard a celebrated vessel, with silver first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded on board' looks like cargo, but only the first letter of loaded is used. HMS Beagle carried Charles Darwin on his voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Beagle is the ship on which Darwin sailed round the world, making it a famous ship.

clue.text: Trustee, skipping troubles, benefits

indicators.note: skipping something means leaving it out

parts.note: travails are troubles or hardships
TR is an abbreviation for trustee

explanation.surface: A trustee who dodges hardship profits from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue order hides it: troubles is the word that loses the trustee's abbreviation from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or advantage, so avails is a verb synonym of benefits.

clue.text: Value in working with valid variety performer

indicators.note: working suggests material being worked over and reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sees the worth of working alongside a legitimate entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' sits inside the clue as a joining word; the letters come from both sides of it. Vaudeville is the American name for music-hall variety shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaudevillian performs in vaudeville, the variety entertainment of songs, comedy and acts.

clue.text: Girl given one sweet drink

parts.note: a lass is a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young woman is handed a sugary drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is an Indian yoghurt drink, often served sweetened, so a sweet drink.

clue.text: Not bad after morning in a frenzy

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the one named second

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning
okay means not bad

explanation.surface: Feeling fine after a morning of wild activity.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave wildly and out of control, so amok is an adverb meaning in a frenzy.

clue.text: Excellent beginning, but not ending

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, star means outstanding, as in a star pupil, so excellent.

clue.text: Scientific study of blood overlooking blood group in clusters

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the final one

parts.note: mats are tangled clusters, as of hair

parts.note: haematic means relating to blood
A is one of the blood groups

explanation.surface: A haematology study looks at blood but somehow ignores blood types.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only 'Scientific study'; 'of blood' starts the wordplay, as an adjective meaning relating to blood.

clue.text: Copy recording, deleting first item

indicators.note: deleting the first item removes the opening letter

parts.note: a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: Making a duplicate of a recording but erasing its first track.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to imitate, as apes were thought to mimic people, so it means to copy.

clue.text: Stark rocks in limestone scenery

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bare rocks stand out in a limestone landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a noun in the scene, but it is a verb telling you to shake up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Karst is landscape formed by limestone dissolving, with caves, sinkholes and bare pavements.

clue.text: Daughter isn't adopting team, choosing to follow another?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it in, so the team goes inside

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A daughter refuses to support the family team, preferring a rival club.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic, marked by the question mark: a dissident breaks from the official line to follow another one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident opposes established doctrine, siding with an alternative view rather than the ruling one.
